saml.description: If the SAML Identity Provider Entity ID is left empty, Keycloak performs no Issuer validation on received SAML assertions.
saml.note: This can look like an issuer-validation bug, but it is documented configuration behavior.

saml.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased unless case-sensitive username is enabled.
saml.note: Case-folding can make distinct upstream usernames appear merged by design.

saml.description: First broker login flows can intentionally link a brokered identity to an existing local account based on email or explicit re-authentication.
saml.note: Identity merges during first login are not automatically vulnerabilities; they may be the configured account-linking workflow.

saml.description: Automatically linking an existing user during first broker login without prompting is documented as dangerous but supported.
saml.note: If this flow is intentionally configured, merges by email/username are by design and should not be treated as unexpected collisions.

saml.description: TOTP codes can be reusable within the valid time window depending on OTP policy; TOTP does not inherently remember used passwords unless reusable-code policy forbids reuse.
saml.note: Replay of a TOTP within its validity window is not necessarily a broker flaw.

saml.description: When SAML step-up authentication is not enabled or not fully configured, Keycloak may continue and emit the legacy unspecified AuthnContextClassRef instead of erroring.
saml.note: Absence of requested AuthnContext enforcement can be backward-compatibility behavior rather than a regression.

saml.description: After successful identity-provider login, the browser flow does not continue; extra authentication such as OTP requires a configured Post Login Flow.
saml.note: If SAML login bypasses local MFA without a post-login flow, that is expected configuration behavior rather than a bypass bug.

saml.constraint: For SAML broker I1 signature-validation default tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST leave both config.validateSignature and config.wantAssertionsSigned unset or OFF when testing insecure defaults. The documented behavior says signature validation only happens when 'Validate Signature' is ON and assertion signing is only expected when 'Want Assertions Signed' is enabled. If you pre-enable either flag, the default-insecure test becomes invalid.

For SAML issuer-validation tests, config.idpEntityId is exact-match validation against the assertion Issuer. If 'Identity Provider Entity ID' is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. Therefore, when testing saml_issuer_mismatch, the fuzzer MUST set config.idpEntityId to the trusted IdP entity ID for the control configuration; for the insecure-default test, it MUST intentionally leave it unset. Do NOT assume issuer checking happens by default.

saml_login MUST be preceded by SP-initiated flow initiation against /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider}/login so the fabricated SAMLResponse can carry the correct InResponseTo. The broker documentation shows this login URL as the SAML broker entrypoint. Sending a standalone forged SAMLResponse without initiating the flow will be rejected for protocol reasons, not because security checks worked.

For I1 tests involving envelope-only signatures or unsigned assertions, the fuzzer MUST vary config.wantAssertionsSigned independently from config.validateSignature. 'Validate Signature' controls whether requests/responses from the external IdP are expected to be signed; 'Want Assertions Signed' specifically indicates whether the SP expects a signed Assertion. To test acceptance of response-only signatures, keep signature validation enabled but set assertion-signing expectations according to the scenario.

For I5 audience-binding tests on SAML assertions, the fuzzer MUST configure the SAML client with a known Client ID / SP entity ID and compare assertion Audience against that value. The docs state the SAML client Client ID is the expected issuer value in AuthnRequests and the broker/provider docs state Service Provider Entity ID defaults to the realm base URL unless overridden. Do not treat audience as unconstrained without first determining which SP entity ID is in effect.

For I5 tests of missing Conditions or missing AudienceRestriction, use saml_login variants that remove or alter the assertion Conditions, but keep in mind Keycloak may still accept or reject based on other configured checks. A valid control must use a normal assertion with Conditions and correct Audience. Without a control login, rejection of the attack case cannot be distinguished from broken provider/client setup.

For I2 replay tests, SAML assertions with OneTimeUse or reused Assertion IDs must be submitted twice against the same configured provider and realm. The first login must be a control success. If the first login fails, the second failure is uninterpretable. Use fixed_assertion_id to ensure the exact same Assertion/@ID is replayed.
saml.source: Attack pattern requirements cross-referenced with SAML broker flow docs

saml.constraint: For I3 MFA-bypass-via-binding-rule tests, the fuzzer MUST configure MFA in a post-login or browser flow that actually applies after broker login. The docs explicitly state that browser flow does not continue after successful identity-provider login unless a Post login flow is configured. Therefore, a valid bypass test must compare password login requiring MFA against SAML broker login under the same post-login enforcement point.

Case handling for brokered usernames is configurable. If 'Case-sensitive username' is disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating users, although server usernames are always lower-case. Therefore, I4 case_confusion tests MUST record whether this setting is enabled. A merge between 'Admin' and 'admin' is by design when case-sensitive username is disabled.

Email-based account linking during first broker login can intentionally merge a brokered identity into an existing local account with the same email, depending on the configured First Login Flow authenticators. Therefore, I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross_protocol_identity_merge tests MUST distinguish between by-design linking flows and silent identity collapse. If Confirm Link Existing Account, Verify Existing Account By Email, Automatically Set Existing User, or Detect Existing Broker User are configured, merges may be expected behavior rather than a bug.

The AutoLink/Automatically Set Existing User first-login flow is explicitly documented as dangerous but supported. If this flow is configured, brokered identities can be linked to existing accounts without prompt. The fuzzer MUST treat resulting merges as configuration-driven behavior unless the test specifically targets unsafe default or unsafe admin-configured linking.

Organization-linked IdP group mapping claim matching supports a companion mode flag: 'Regex Claim Values'. When enabled, claim values are treated as regular expressions; when disabled, values must match exactly. For I4/I5 multi-identity tests using Advanced Claim to Group mappers, wildcards or regex-like strings MUST NOT be used unless Regex Claim Values is enabled. Otherwise they are exact literals.

SAML RequestedAuthnContext comparison has explicit modes Exact, Minimum, Maximum, Better, with default Exact. For step-up or MFA-related SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST set the intended comparison mode explicitly when relying on RequestedAuthnContext semantics. Do not assume non-exact matching unless configured.

Numeric sentinel: Password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses -1 as a sentinel meaning 'use algorithm default iterations', not disable. Never interpret -1 as turning hashing off. The actual default depends on the selected algorithm.
Numeric sentinel: Password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses 0 as a sentinel meaning 'always re-authenticate before password update', not unlimited. Never interpret 0 as disable.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn policy 'Timeout' uses 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation, not necessarily immediate expiry and not disable. Never assume 0 means zero-second timeout.
Numeric sentinel: User session limits use 0 to disable the session-count check for both realm and client session limits. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions.

Numeric sentinel: authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 authentication sub-sessions per root authentication session, and when the limit is reached the oldest sub-session is removed. This is not a hard failure. Multi-tab or repeated SP-initiated login tests can evict older auth sub-sessions and cause confusing flow restarts.

create_tenant returns 201 with no body — the realm/tenant name is the value you provided in params, not a response field. Do NOT use captures for the resource name; reference the params value directly in subsequent events.

For SAML issuer-validation tests (I1 saml_issuer_mismatch), create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST set config.idpEntityId. Documentation states that if Identity Provider Entity ID is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. A login accepted with idpEntityId unset is a configuration default issue, not proof that issuer checking is bypassed when configured.

For SAML signature-validation default tests (I1 saml_cert_substitution, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), the fuzzer MUST distinguish Validate Signature from Want Assertions Signed. Validate Signature controls whether Keycloak expects signed SAML requests/responses from the external IdP; Want Assertions Signed controls whether the SP expects a signed Assertion specifically. To test insecure defaults, create the provider with default config and do NOT set config.validateSignature=true or config.wantAssertionsSigned=true.

For assertion-level integrity tests (I1 saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), config.wantAssertionsSigned MUST be enabled when testing whether unsigned assertions are rejected. Otherwise Keycloak may accept a signed response envelope without requiring an individually signed assertion by configuration.

For trust-anchor tests against SAML signatures (I1 saml_cert_substitution), if config.useMetadataDescriptorUrl is OFF then signature validation uses config.signingCertificate. If useMetadataDescriptorUrl is ON, certificates are downloaded and cached from config.metadataDescriptorUrl. The fuzzer MUST know which trust source is active; otherwise a passing or failing signature test may reflect stale cached metadata rather than current provider config.

For SAML audience-binding tests (I5 saml_wrong_audience, saml_no_audience_restriction, saml_no_conditions), configure the brokered SAML flow against a concrete SP entity ID. The Service Provider Entity ID defaults to the realm base URL if not set. Tests that forge Audience values must compare against the effective SP entity ID actually used by Keycloak, not an assumed client identifier.

For SAML principal-binding tests (I4), config.principalType determines which assertion field identifies the external user: Subject NameID or a SAML attribute. The fuzzer MUST record which principal source is configured before interpreting collisions. A NameID/email mismatch only proves a vulnerability if the configured principal source should have selected the non-colliding field.

For I4 multi-identity tests, config.principalAttribute is exact-name selection of the identifying SAML attribute; the documentation describes choosing the attribute by name or friendly name and does not describe wildcard or regex matching. Do NOT set principalAttribute='*' expecting wildcard behavior. To vary identities across different attributes, omit principalAttribute by using Subject NameID principal type or set an exact attribute name consistently.

For organization-linked IdP group mapping tests, Advanced Claim to Group supports a companion flag 'Regex Claim Values'. When disabled, claim values must match exactly; when enabled, values are treated as regular expressions. For I4 multi-user scenarios, exact-match claim values MUST be omitted or varied explicitly; using '*' without regex mode matches only the literal asterisk.

For I3 config-change sequences involving broker settings, NEW logins after admin changes are expected to use the updated configuration by design. A valid coherence test must show that the same SAML input is evaluated differently only because configuration changed between attempts, not treat the config change itself as a bug.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule, MFA enforcement after broker login depends on the configured Post Login Flow. Documentation states the browser flow does not continue after successful identity-provider login; additional steps such as OTP require a Post login flow. Therefore the fuzzer MUST configure the IdP with postBrokerLoginFlowAlias pointing to a flow that enforces MFA before claiming bypass.

For first-login collision tests (I4 saml_email_binding_collision, cross_protocol_identity_merge), the result is heavily affected by the selected First Login Flow. Default first broker login may create a new user, prompt for linking, or require re-authentication depending on authenticators. The fuzzer MUST control firstBrokerLoginFlowAlias and interpret merges only relative to that flow.

The AutoLink/Automatically Set Existing User first-login configuration is documented as dangerous and can automatically link existing accounts by email/username without verification. If such a flow is configured, cross-account merges are by design and MUST be recorded as known setup behavior, not an I4 vulnerability.

Case handling for brokered usernames is configurable. General IdP config 'Case-sensitive username' affects the federated username associated with the identity provider; otherwise usernames from the IdP are lower-cased, while server usernames are always lower-case. For I4 case_confusion tests, the fuzzer MUST note whether case-sensitive username is enabled; otherwise Admin vs admin collapsing may be by design.

For I4 email-based merge tests, Trust Email changes first-login behavior by marking brokered emails as verified and can affect linking flows. The fuzzer MUST keep trustEmail fixed across control and attack cases; otherwise differences may reflect trusted-email onboarding behavior rather than principal-binding flaws.

For SAML replay tests (I2 saml_one_time_use_replay and saml_assertion_id_replay), use TWO saml_login events with the SAME fixed_assertion_id. For OneTimeUse, also include include_onetimeuse=true in both requests. The first login is the control and should succeed; only the second login determines replay handling.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, 30 minutes by default. SAML broker flows are session-bound and multi-step. The fuzzer MUST complete SP-initiated flow initiation and ACS submission within the same live authentication session; otherwise failures are expired-session artifacts, not I3 coherence bugs.

Keycloak may automatically restart authentication in other browser tabs after one tab authenticates, due to login-page JavaScript and existing SSO session. Multi-tab or repeated browser-flow tests must isolate sessions/cookies; otherwise a second SAML attempt may succeed via SSO restart rather than by reprocessing the forged assertion.

User session limits can deny or terminate sessions during broker login only if the User Session Count Limiter authenticator is added to the Browser flow, Direct Grant flow, Reset Credentials flow, and Post Broker Login flow. If not configured in Post Broker Login flow, SAML logins may bypass intended session-limit enforcement by design.

Numeric sentinel: password policy 'Hashing iterations' uses -1 as a sentinel meaning use the algorithm default iteration count, not literal negative one and not disable hashing. Defaults are algorithm-specific (for example argon2=5, pbkdf2-sha512=210000, pbkdf2-sha256=600000, pbkdf2=1300000). Never interpret -1 as disabling the check.

Numeric sentinel: password policy 'Maximum Authentication Age' uses 0 as a sentinel meaning the user must always re-authenticate before updating the password. It is not 'use default' and not 'disable re-authentication'.

Numeric sentinel: WebAuthn policy Timeout uses 0 to delegate timeout behavior to the authenticator/browser implementation. It is not guaranteed to mean immediate expiry and not guaranteed to disable timeout checks.
Numeric sentinel: user session count limiter uses 0 to disable the realm session limit or client session limit check. It is not a literal zero-session allowance.

Numeric sentinel: authenticationSessions SPI authSessionsLimit defaults to 300 sub-sessions per root authentication session, and when the limit is reached the oldest authentication sub-session is removed on new requests. This is eviction behavior, not hard failure. Tests that open many parallel auth attempts must avoid hitting this limit or they may lose the original SAML flow state.

For I5 authorization tests using client scopes, a client scope with role scope mappings applies only if the user is permitted to use it, meaning there must be an intersection between user roles and client-scope roles. Missing claims or scopes in tokens may be due to client-scope permission filtering, not broker under-issuance.

For I5 scope-escalation style tests on Keycloak-issued tokens after SAML login, role scope mappings limit roles in tokens to the intersection of user roles and client role-scope mappings. By default, clients have full scope allowed. The fuzzer MUST explicitly tighten client scope mappings when testing overbroad grants; otherwise broad role issuance is default behavior.

For organization claim tests, the organization scope has exact request semantics: 'organization' maps one organization, 'organization:<alias>' maps the named organization, and 'organization:*' maps all organizations. These are fixed formats, not wildcard matching on arbitrary aliases. Use the documented forms exactly.

For SAML step-up tests, RequestedAuthnContext comparison supports Exact, Minimum, Maximum, or Better. The selected comparison changes which AuthnContextClassRef values satisfy the request. The fuzzer MUST set and track authnContextComparisonType; otherwise a successful login may satisfy a weaker or alternate context by design.

For SAML step-up tests, if the step-up-authentication-saml feature is not enabled, or no URI/LoA mapping exists, or the AuthnContextClassRef mapper is not executed, Keycloak preserves backward compatibility by returning 'unspecified' instead of erroring. Do not flag this as an I1/I5 failure unless the feature and mappings are explicitly configured.

create_tenant returns success with no response body. The realm name is the value provided in the request body, not a response field. Do NOT use captures for the realm identifier; reference the input realm parameter directly in subsequent events.

For SAML broker I1 default-signature tests, create_provider/enable_auth_method MUST leave config.validateSignature unset or OFF and MUST leave config.wantAssertionsSigned unset or OFF when testing insecure defaults. The documented defaults do not require signature validation unless explicitly enabled; setting them ON converts the test into a hardened configuration and masks default-acceptance bugs.

Identity Provider Entity ID performs exact issuer validation only when configured. If config.idpEntityId is empty, no Issuer validation is performed. For saml_issuer_mismatch tests, the fuzzer MUST set config.identity_provider_entity_id to the trusted IdP entity ID in the provider config for the control case, and use saml_login with idp_entity_id='https://wrong-issuer.example/idp' for the attack. For the insecure-default test, omit config.identity_provider_entity_id entirely; acceptance then is BY CONFIGURATION, not proof of correct issuer checking.

Want Assertions Signed and Validate Signature are independent SAML broker settings. Want Assertions Signed indicates the SP expects a signed Assertion; Validate Signature indicates requests/responses from the external IdP are expected to be digitally signed. For unsigned-assertion and spurious-signature tests, the fuzzer MUST vary these explicitly and not assume one implies the other.

For SAML POST-binding integrity tests, use saml_login against /realms/{realm}/broker/{provider}/endpoint with POST form data. Keycloak documents SAML broker ACS as POST-based and all SAML bindings use the SAML endpoint family; do not test ACS with GET or OIDC callback semantics.

Principal Type controls which SAML assertion field identifies the external user: Subject NameID or a SAML attribute by name/friendly name. For I4 collision tests, the fuzzer MUST know which principal source is configured. If Principal Type uses Subject NameID, varying email alone may not change the bound principal. If Principal Type uses attribute, varying NameID alone may not change the bound principal.

Case-sensitive username is a broker setting with security impact. If disabled, usernames from the identity provider are lower-cased when federating; usernames in the server are always lower-case. Therefore case_confusion tests using 'Admin' vs 'admin' can collapse by design unless this setting is enabled. The fuzzer MUST record this setting before flagging I4 collisions.

Trust Email can cause first-login linking behavior to rely on brokered email trust. For saml_email_binding_collision and cross_protocol_identity_merge tests, the fuzzer MUST test with Trust Email both OFF and ON where possible, and MUST distinguish email-trusted linking behavior from principal-binding behavior.

First Login Flow materially changes account-linking semantics. Default first broker login may create a new user, prompt to link an existing account, verify by email, or require re-authentication. Automatically Set Existing User / AutoLink flows can link without verification and are explicitly documented as dangerous. The fuzzer MUST capture which first login flow is configured before interpreting identity merges as vulnerabilities.

For I3 saml_mfa_bypass_via_binding_rule tests, a valid sequence MUST compare the same user authenticating through password flow versus SAML broker flow while a Post login flow or first-login re-authentication/MFA step is configured. Documentation states browser flow does not continue after IdP login unless Post login flow is configured. Therefore, SAML login without a post-login MFA step may bypass local MFA by configuration, not by bug.

Requested AuthnContext constraints are optional. If no ClassRefs or DeclRefs are present, the Identity Provider does not enforce additional constraints. For SAML step-up or MFA-strength tests, the fuzzer MUST configure authn_context_class_refs or authn_context_decl_refs explicitly; otherwise absence of stronger authentication is by design.

SAML client Valid Redirect URIs support wildcards only at the end of a URL pattern. This is URL matching for ACS fallback, not identity matching. Do not reuse redirect URI wildcard assumptions for principal or issuer constraints.

Include OneTimeUse Condition on SAML clients is an explicit switch. Replay tests against Keycloak as IdP or SP behavior MUST not assume OneTimeUse is always present. For broker replay tests, the attack assertion must explicitly include OneTimeUse when testing enforcement; absence of enforcement on assertions without that condition is not sufficient evidence of a replay bug.

Authentication sessions expire after the realm Login timeout, usually 30 minutes by default. Multi-step SAML browser flows are session-bound; if the SP-initiated flow expires before the forged SAMLResponse is posted, failures are due to expired authentication session rather than signature or issuer validation. The fuzzer MUST keep SP-initiation and ACS submission within the authentication-session lifetime.

User session count limiter uses numeric sentinel 0 = disabled for both realm session limit and client session limit. Never interpret 0 as literal zero allowed sessions. If testing session-limit side effects around SAML logins, configure nonzero values explicitly.
Password policy Maximum Authentication Age uses numeric sentinel 0 = always re-authenticate before password update. Never interpret 0 as 'use default' or 'disabled'.
Password policy Hashing iterations uses numeric sentinel -1 = use algorithm default iterations, not disable hashing or zero iterations. Never assume -1 disables the underlying check.
WebAuthn timeout uses numeric sentinel 0 = behavior depends on authenticator implementation, not strict zero timeout. Never use 0 as a deterministic expiry boundary in MFA-related tests.
SAML assertion lifespan on clients has sentinel behavior: if not specified, realm Access Token Lifespan is used. Do not assume omission means unlimited assertion validity.

OTP policy Reusable code defaults to non-reusable. TOTP validity still spans the configured token period and look-around window, and documentation notes TOTP reuse within the valid interval is possible unless explicitly prevented by reusable-code policy. The fuzzer MUST distinguish OTP reuse semantics from SAML assertion replay semantics.

For I5 authorization tests involving roles/groups in tokens or assertions, Keycloak role scope mappings limit roles included in issued tokens/assertions to the intersection of user roles and client scope mappings. Missing roles in downstream tokens may be due to client scope configuration rather than broker under-grant or over-grant behavior.

Organization group mapping via IdP mappers supports exact match by default and regex only when Regex Claim Values is enabled. For multi-identity tests, exact-match claim mappings MUST be omitted rather than set to wildcard-like values unless regex mode is explicitly enabled.

Regex-based authorization policy uses Java regular expressions on Target Claim. This is regex matching, not exact matching. Tests that expect literal matching MUST avoid regex metacharacters unless intentionally testing regex behavior.

Group-based authorization policy obtains groups either from a configured Groups Claim in the token or from realm configuration if Groups Claim is undefined. For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, the fuzzer MUST control whether evaluation uses token groups or server-side group membership; otherwise results are ambiguous.

Role-based authorization policy defaults to using roles available from the token; if Fetch Roles is enabled, it ignores token roles and checks any role associated with the user instead. For I5 tests about token-bounded authorization, Fetch Roles MUST remain disabled, otherwise server-side roles can make a narrowed token appear over-authorized by design.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
